metrics.method: Full history read message-by-message (122 lines, 112 non-service messages, 2026-08-03 to 2026-09-17; client = alias 'Alanna<3' per config/clients.yaml, all other senders = ALTR per config/team.yaml). client_questions_total counts distinct client messages that required an ALTR response (direct questions, instructions, scheduling requests and bulk content handovers): msgs #21, #22, #24, #39, #54, #62, #70, #74, #92, #105, #108. unanswered_over_24h counts those that never received a substantive reply within 24h: #70 (live-stream pause instruction, never answered, 30 days), #105 (5000+ photo handover, 3.8 days to a three-word 'Thank you Alanna' that also covered two later uploads, no plan ever), and the Aug 17/24/29 portion of #22 (never confirmed, 32 days); the 9/12-9/13 sexting sets waited 30h for the same three-word reply and are counted inside #105's acknowledgement. Answered questions were typically fast — 1 minute to 14 hours, median ~5h — so the failure is selective, not slow. max_team_silence_days = longest gap between consecutive non-service ALTR messages: 2026-08-17T19:31 to 2026-08-26T19:17 = 8.99 days, which contains her 8/19 instruction. Promises = explicit forward commitments made by ALTR in chat; kept = visibly delivered in chat or confirmed by the client (intros, 8/3 scene sent out, invoicing starting 8/15, custom domain built, 9/1 invoice on the promised date, 9/14 pre-invoice heads-up); lapsed = never delivered or never closed (page audit, impersonator takedown confirmation, weekly leak reports, 'push heavy' on customs, new IG account, weekly creative ideas, kickoff call, FAQ form chase, promo reel pipeline, Aug 17/24/29 drops).

what_client_wanted: Her scenes released on time, at 7pm LA — her stated #1 priority, volunteered with five dates on day one and reconfirmed unprompted: 'Correct 10th 7pm La time' (8/10) and 'Yes 7pm for all releases' (8/12). Three of those five dates were never covered.

Her content actually posted. Four bulk handovers in six weeks: 'All my social and of content' (8/3), 'Heyyy I uploaded 5000+ new photos to post on my wall and x' (9/10), 'New squirting sexting set' (9/12), 'Hey, I have two new sexting sets' (9/13). Not one was ever confirmed as ingested or scheduled.

More Instagram reach, while keeping her hands on the wheel: 'Would it possible to start more instas for me?' and 'I’m already running a lot myself' (8/31), then 'I have 3 but just run them myself' (9/16) — she wants growth delivered for her, not her logins taken off her.

To be useful and fast, and to have leaks handled: 'the chatters can always message me and I’ll do it super quick' (8/7), 'Any new customs or try to sell heaps I’ll do them in the next few days' (8/15), 'Let me know what I need to do to get on top of my leaks' (8/12).
what_worked: The chatting itself earned unprompted praise in week one — 'Loving the chatting so far' / 'It sounds so good' (8/8). This is the only spontaneous compliment in the account's history and it came from the service that has since gone silent.

Ollie's first ten days were real account management and she responded to every bit of it: a same-day check-in on each drop ('Hey @alannaapow the lily and francis 3some is going live today right?', 8/10), a conversion consult on her trailer ('Do you mind if we give this a go for this drop with the twitter trailer for the campaign?', 8/4 — she replied 'Yes sounds good'), and a transparent explanation of the Tip $5 campaign structure ('the tapes are not being sold for $5'). This is the template; it simply stopped.

Stephski's 9/14 pre-invoice cash-flow heads-up — 'Just letting you know your invoice will be sent tomorrow, so it would be great if you could initiate a OF withdrawl today so the funds hit your account in time!' — is the first time anyone worked this client's timing instead of just reminding her, and is worth copying agency-wide. Mica's 9/17 Instagram security advisory, including 'do not send your backup codes to anyone, including our team', is the same instinct applied to protecting her.
top_fix: Give every account one named owner who is accountable for a weekly written recap to the client and a 24-hour acknowledgement on every handover she sends — not 'thank you', but what was received, where it went and when it posts. Every severe gap on this account is the same missing habit: three scene drops, 5000 photos, three sexting sets, the customs promise, the new IG account, the impersonator takedown and the weekly leak reports all failed not because anyone refused her, but because nothing she handed us was ever closed out loud, and with no recap cadence nobody noticed her 80% engagement drop or that she has stopped asking us for anything.
